findings.rationale: GU (n_train 708, small, so its statistics are noisy) is the only client flagged by several independent screens that point the same way. (1) client_updates: median update norm is inflated (z=+4.6, the highest of any client after size adjustment). In rounds 11-19 its norm ratio is 1.07-1.98 and its cosine to the median swings between about -0.8 and +0.6, with no stable direction, which is the signature of large random noise in uploads. Its federation-wide mean cosine (0.226) is the lowest of all clients. (2) client_performance: round-20 CITL is -0.072 (z=-3.2), a weaker second signal. (3) drift_by_round: the largest feature shift is 2.9 federation SDs (Sex), flagged z=+3.3. Caveats: evidence is moderate, each z is below the ~6 threshold, and the per-round values are noisy because the client is small. Early rounds (1-10) look more normal, so onset is estimated at round 11. Independently, attribution_churn shows persistent late-round explanation jitter (rank correlation 0.09-0.4 in rounds 15-20). That is consistent with this fault but does not identify the client.

report.summary: I screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), and then ran confirmation queries and attribution_churn. The budget is now fully spent (0 left). Most anomalies sat at |z| of about 3-5, which is what chance produces across 52 clients and dozens of statistics, and most did not reproduce on re-query. Examples: WV's AnyHealthcare and Smoker percentile outliers and VI's Stroke-mean outlier both looked normal on re-query. Remaining unconfirmed leads, which I did not report: MO's update norm declines steadily from about 1.0 (round 1) to 0.13 (round 20), with cosine to the median falling toward 0 after about round 10 (norm z=-4.7; it may be a free-rider or converging-client pattern, but it does not match a clean fault signature and no second tool confirmed it). WA (Income group 1, O/E 10.8) and NY (Income group 2, O/E 3.6) show subgroup over-prediction outliers at z_noise of about 3.2-3.4. These are the opposite direction from under-diagnosis, and no FNR outliers appeared. The only finding I report is GU, at low-to-moderate confidence (0.35), for explanation_instability: its uploads are inflated and erratic from about round 11, and the evidence rests on several tools at |z| of about 3-5. The federation is otherwise consistent with clean. The GU finding could be a false alarm, and I could not spend budget to verify it further.
